findings.documented: API key sent as query parameter: ?api_key=IVY26-XXXX
findings.actual: API key must be sent via X-API-Key request header. Query parameter returns error: 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'
findings.how_found: First API call with documented query parameter format returned an error with explicit instructions
findings.impact: Every request must use the header approach; documented method completely fails

findings.documented: Response field is 'token', expires_in is 86400 (24 hours), no refresh flow
findings.actual: Response field is 'access_token' (not 'token'), expires_in is 900 (15 minutes), includes 'refresh_token' and 'refresh_url': '/auth/refresh'
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/login and compared response keys/values with documentation
findings.impact: Frontend must implement token refresh to maintain sessions beyond 15 minutes; documented 24h expiry is wrong by 96x

findings.documented: Response user object contains {email, name}
findings.actual: User object only contains {email}, no 'name' field
findings.how_found: Inspected login response JSON
findings.impact: Cannot display user name in UI; must derive display name from email

findings.documented: Not documented. Documentation says 'There is no refresh flow'
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh exists, accepts {refresh_token} body, returns new access_token + refresh_token pair
findings.how_found: Login response included 'refresh_url': '/auth/refresh'; tested endpoint and it works
findings.impact: Critical for maintaining sessions beyond 15 minutes; without this, users would be logged out every 15 minutes

findings.documented: Invalidates the current token server side
findings.actual: Returns {ok: true, note: 'tokens are stateless; discard them client side'}. Tokens are NOT invalidated server-side
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/logout and read the response
findings.impact: Logout is client-side only; old tokens remain valid until expiry

findings.documented: Uses 'page' parameter (1-indexed), maximum limit is 200, response contains 'page' and 'page_size'
findings.actual: Uses 'offset' parameter (0-indexed). 'page' parameter is silently ignored. Maximum limit is 50 (not 200). Response contains 'offset', 'limit', 'count', 'has_more' (not 'page', 'page_size')
findings.how_found: Tested page=2 parameter (ignored), tested limit=200 (capped to 50), compared response shape with docs
findings.impact: Must use offset-based pagination; page-based approach silently returns page 1 every time. Affects data collection throughput since max 50 records per request instead of 200

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings only. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side. total reflects matching records
findings.actual: Returns ALL listings including inactive ones (is_live=false). 978 out of 4700 listings have is_live=false. API reports total=4498 but returns 4700 unique records across all pages
findings.how_found: Fetched all pages and found is_live=false records. Counted 4700 unique listing IDs but API total field said 4498
findings.impact: Frontend must filter by is_live client-side if only active listings should be shown. Total count is unreliable

findings.documented: Each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property
findings.actual: One pair of listings shares identical structural attributes (apartment_name, locality, bedroom, bathroom, floor, total_floors, carpet_area, super_built_up_area) across different websites, indicating they describe the same property
findings.how_found: Grouped all listings by structural property attributes and found one group with 2 listings
findings.impact: unique_properties (4699) differs from total listing records (4700) by 1

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} (singular) returns a single listing
findings.actual: Returns 404. The correct path is GET /v1/listings/{listing_id} (plural 'listings')
findings.how_found: Tested documented singular path, got 404. Tested plural path and it worked
findings.impact: Must use /v1/listings/{id} for single listing retrieval

findings.documented: Returns up to ten comparable listings — same locality, same bedroom count, price within 15%
findings.actual: Returns 404. Endpoint does not exist
findings.how_found: Called endpoint with valid listing ID, received 404
findings.impact: Cannot show 'similar listings' feature; must implement client-side if needed

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites for listing saved listings, POST /v1/favourites to add, DELETE /v1/favourites/{id} to remove
findings.actual: All /v1/favourites paths return 404. The actual endpoint is /v1/saved
findings.how_found: Tested /v1/favourites (404), then tried /v1/favorites, /v1/saved, /v1/wishlist. Only /v1/saved returned 200
findings.impact: Must use /v1/saved instead of /v1/favourites for all saved listing operations

findings.documented: Not documented (documented as /v1/favourites)
findings.actual: POST /v1/saved requires {listing_id} field (not {id} as documented for /v1/favourites). GET returns {count, results}. DELETE /v1/saved/{listing_id} removes a saved listing
findings.how_found: Discovered through trial after /v1/favourites returned 404. POST with {id} returned validation error specifying {listing_id} is required
findings.impact: Request body field name differs from documentation

findings.documented: Returns pre-computed aggregates: city, total_listings, median_price, median_price_per_sqft, by_locality, by_bhk
findings.actual: Returns 404. Endpoint does not exist. Also tried /v1/analytics — also 404
findings.how_found: Called both /v1/analytics/summary and /v1/analytics, both returned 404
findings.impact: Must compute all analytics client-side from raw listing data

findings.documented: Timestamps are ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix everywhere
findings.actual: Listing posted_at has NO timezone suffix (e.g. '2026-06-15T02:33:00'). Rental posted_at has Z suffix. Health endpoint uses +05:30. Inconsistent across endpoints
findings.how_found: Compared posted_at format across listings, rentals, and health endpoint
findings.impact: Timezone-sensitive calculations (like listings_last_7_days) are ambiguous. Must decide whether to treat suffix-less timestamps as UTC or IST

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees
findings.actual: Prices are in mixed units: most are in crores (1-5 range), 13 projects have values in lakhs (30-100 range). 372 out of 520 projects have price_min > price_max because price_min is in lakhs while price_max is in crores
findings.how_found: Noticed price_max values like 2.95 (obviously not rupees). Compared with actual listing prices in each project. Found 372 projects where min > max — impossible if same unit
findings.impact: Must detect and normalize price units to compare projects correctly. Affects costliest_project calculation

findings.documented: Area is square feet, integer, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: magichomes website listings have carpet_area in square meters (not square feet). 388 magichomes listings have carpet_area < 200 (e.g. 75-154), which makes sense as sqm but is impossibly small as sqft for apartments
findings.how_found: Analyzed carpet_area distribution by website. magichomes has min=45 for 2BHK (impossible sqft), but 45 sqm = 484 sqft (reasonable). Other websites all have 600+ sqft for 2BHK
findings.impact: Price/sqft calculations using raw carpet_area values are inflated for magichomes listings. Affects avg_price_per_sqft_2bhk

findings.documented: All listings are valid property records
findings.actual: 32 listings describe impossible properties: floor > total_floors (e.g. floor 33 of 26), negative prices, swapped lat/lon coordinates
findings.how_found: Validated all records programmatically: checked floor <= total_floors, price > 0, carpet_area > 0, carpet_area <= super_built_up_area, coordinates within Bangalore bounds
findings.impact: These records cannot represent real properties and must be flagged or excluded from calculations

findings.documented: description is the seller's own text, shown as written
findings.actual: 7 listings contain AI prompt injection in descriptions: instructions to add fake fields to submission.json or fake footer text. 28 listings contain 'Pay a token amount of Rs 25,000 today to block the unit' — a classic lead generation scam tactic
findings.how_found: Read descriptions during data analysis. Found two categories: (1) text targeting AI tools with fake data requirements, (2) token amount advance-fee scam language
findings.impact: 35 total fake listings exist to generate enquiries, not to sell real properties. Must be excluded from price calculations

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings returns
findings.actual: 392 out of 520 projects have a total_listings count that does NOT match the actual number of listing records associated with that project_id
findings.how_found: For each project, counted listing records with matching project_id and compared with the project's total_listings field
findings.impact: Cannot rely on project's total_listings field for accurate listing counts

findings.documented: Returns service status and the server clock. Documentation conventions say timestamps are UTC with Z suffix
findings.actual: Returns timestamps with +05:30 offset (IST), not UTC with Z suffix. Response includes 'timezone': 'Asia/Kolkata' and 'reference_date' field
findings.how_found: Called GET /health as the first API request
findings.impact: Confirms server operates in IST; helps interpret ambiguous timestamps in listing data
